scope: Independent final worker/controller delta review and sealed CPU proof verification; not device execution or live admission.
reviewed_behavior: Unchanged p197 owner launch, namespace admission, unlimited address-space check, serialized bounded journal monitoring, incident SIGTERM-once and retained process/lease/drain failure behavior.
Each RUN and each SAVE/RELEASE has independent before/after fault/admission guards: 32 operation boundaries across 8 requests and 8 controls.
Same-generation resume SAVE supplies original prompt plus saved 256 output IDs plus new 128 output IDs; append SAVE supplies full canonical 469-token prompt plus reply.
SAVE acknowledgement must match operation receipt and manifest hash; checkpoint exists only after completed reply; native transport validates whole visible history.
Exactly five saves and three releases, fixed control IDs, experimental v1.2+p198 labels and current device binary identity; append/repeat/fresh state equality.
Final release required before draining, exactly 8 completed controls and requests, no discarded pending state, clean native stop/exit/FD drain.
Controller independently checks final counts/control order/correctness and reserves 27GB plus800MB planned writes before stopping endpoints.
Frozen one-stop endpoint window and per-operation guarded restoration retained; external PAUSE bytes preserved on incident; no retries or setting changes.
limitations: Actual device lifecycle, runtime fault review and live admission remain coordinator-owned and have not been performed by this audit.
CPU host proof used six saves/two releases to exercise final SAVE; device pilot intentionally uses five saves/three releases with final RELEASE.
No throughput record, general serving, HTTP endpoint or parking adapter is qualified.
